changes.summary: record native outcomes and retire pending generated work
changes.body:
Generated run, visit and group closure now records versioned succeeded, failed
or cancelled facts in native `close_reason`. Original `{choice,data}` is preserved;
a completed review choosing changes is still successful execution. Derived
`workflow-outcome:*` labels support native filtering; projection failures are
explicit and never replace native closure authority.

Add reason-required `busybee settle RUN cancel|fail --reason TEXT` for pending generated
scope. It preserves completed work and source acceptance, refuses unfinished manual descendants, human/HITL or other-agent
reservations and unsupported inventory, and requires owning-host execution clearance unless
explicit unmanaged provenance proves that no managed execution was exposed.
Partial effects retain fences and evidence; settlement neither stops workers
nor recovers held locks. Existing navigation commands remain unchanged.

Settlement leaves saved chart state unchanged. Its fences require cooperating
version-matched tools on one live database; they do not fence concurrent tracker
exchange or arbitrary native edits.

adoption.text:
use matching Busy Bee, Bee and Colony versions on the same live
database; coordinate active work before refreshing the Colony daemon. Consumers
that interpret `close_reason` or equate closure with success must use the native
outcome contract. Inspect retained partial effects before recovery, not replay.
read `busybee settle --help` before explicitly authorized retirement.

changes.summary: label generated workflow work for filtering
changes.body:
New workflow run, grouping and stage beads carry `busybee-workflow`. This
classification leaves access, assignment and routing unchanged. Ordinary parent
work and workflow system beads retain their existing labels.

adoption.text:
explicitly backfill existing workflow run, grouping and stage beads
from saved workflow records to include historical work in label-based views.
New creation labels do not backfill existing records.

changes.summary: remove the hourly work-review workflow catalog
changes.body:
Remove this repository's `blocked-review` and `in-progress-review` workflows
and their shared work-review module. Busy Bee's general workflow execution,
saved outcomes and run completion remain unchanged.
breaking: The `blocked-review` and `in-progress-review` definitions and their shared module are removed from Hive's workflow catalogue. Saved runs that depend on them can no longer restore from this checkout.

adoption.text:
update catalog callers and configuration that select either removed
workflow. Inspect unfinished runs and their workers before adopting this
checkout; the removed definitions are no longer available for restoration.
Keep any disposition of saved runs and workers explicit. This change neither
migrates nor automatically closes existing runs.

changes.summary: add focused blocked and in-progress review workflows
changes.body:
Hive's workflow catalogue now includes `blocked-review` and `in-progress-review`.
Each accounts for every frozen candidate before an optional bounded recovery
stage. Typed outcomes preserve candidate fingerprints, review tokens and exact
predecessor request IDs. Cancelled recovery targets carry native continuation
references for the workflow to assess. Recovery results distinguish submitted
replacements from deferred cases and retain replacement and reopened task IDs.

Optional: adopt these workflows for Colony's automatic work reviews.

Required when enabling: provide both definitions, their shared workflow helper
and dependencies in the execution checkout. These definitions use ordinary Busy Bee
progression, response delivery and saved-run completion; `busybee init` does not
install them.

changes.summary: simplify repository workflows and separate authoring guidance
changes.body:
Hive's `do-feature-task` 0.2.0 uses prepare, work, independent review and local
delivery. Its input contains `canonicalRoot`, `base` and `isolation`; the source
task retains the assignment and authorization. Land 5.0.0 uses check,
review, finish, verify and local-update, removes `expectedCommits` and receipt
payloads, and accepts evidence-bearing outcomes. Both preserve distinct
review visits and return findings or changed content through checks and
renewed review. These versions break compatibility with their prior saved
states, context and outcome contracts.

Do Work 1.0.1 and Release 3.0.0 shorten instructions without changing their
input or outcome contracts. Release retains source landing before tagging,
checksum verification before formula landing, and its final tracker
publication checkpoint. `busybee init` now reports the version from its
bundled manifest instead of a fixed value.

`workflow-authoring` is now an independently discoverable bundled skill.
The `workflow-execution/references/authoring.md` resource is removed.

Required: before adopting the changed repository definitions, inspect
unfinished runs with `busybee preflight` and follow the documented
same-scope recovery procedure for incompatible runs, retaining prior work
and evidence. Read `busybee input-schema` for new input and `busybee discover` for
active outcomes; update callers using removed fields or choices.

Required: replace calls to
`busybee skills file workflow-execution references/authoring.md` with
`busybee skills get workflow-authoring`.
Definitions remain checkout-owned; upgrading the executable does not
replace an existing repository catalogue.
breaking: simplify repository workflows and separate authoring guidance

changes.summary: omit context and instructions from default run views
changes.body:
The public `run`, `start`, `show`, `collect`, `next` and `choice` commands
omit `active[].context` and `active[].instructions` from their default
output. Run status, task IDs, titles, commands, request IDs, actor paths
and generated visit references remain available.

`busybee show RUN --instructions --json` adds each active visit's exact
saved instruction text without rerendering it or exposing actor context.
Runtime APIs, saved checkpoints and native task descriptions are unchanged.

Required: update consumers that expect either omitted field. Read the full
native run brief with `br show RUN --json` on entry and each active task
brief with `br show TASK --json` once per visit; refresh them when relevant
scope, state or authority changes, or required context is missing. Use
compact run views between these reads, `busybee discover RUN --json` for
outcome schemas and `busybee show RUN --instructions --json` when frozen
instruction text is needed. Remove reliance on `active[].context` for work
details; use the native brief. See `busybee show --help` for the contract.
breaking: omit context and instructions from default run views

changes.summary: follow replacements of cancelled stage requests
changes.body:
Collection follows native replacement provenance from a cancelled Bee-dispatched
stage to its actual replacement. Pending replacement work remains pending; a
genuine closed-stage result advances the original run. The saved run and visit
remain intact, and ambiguous replacement links still fail explicitly.

Optional: use `bee retry --help` for deliberate cancellation resumption, then
continue the existing run with `busybee collect RUN --json`. Cancellation does
not trigger automatic resumption.

Required: upgrade Busy Bee together with Bee before collecting stages resumed
with `--resume-cancelled`; an older Busy Bee does not follow cancelled-request
replacement provenance.

changes.summary: move driver admission into system tooling
changes.body:
Bee's driver admission integration uses `busybee system prepare-driver RUN --json`;
the former top-level path is removed. Like the other system interfaces, this
operation requires `--json`. Busy Bee dispatches stage workers through
`bee system dispatch-stage`.

Required: upgrade Busy Bee with Bee and Colony so both integration directions use
the matching paths. Update custom driver-admission callers to include `system`
and `--json`. Ordinary orphan recovery uses `bee attach-workflow`; failed drivers
use `bee retry`.
breaking: move driver admission into system tooling

adoption.text:
upgrade Busy Bee with Bee and Colony so both integration directions use
the matching paths. Update custom driver-admission callers to include `system`
and `--json`. Ordinary orphan recovery uses `bee attach-workflow`; failed drivers
use `bee retry`.

changes.body:
Hive's repository workflow catalogue adds `do-feature-task` for isolated,
reviewed local integration into a named feature base. Exact candidate
approval, stale-base repair, partial-effect inspection and post-done source
closure keep native prerequisites from releasing early. Native reconstruction
requires a matching recorded uncertainty origin for the current candidate.

Optional: adopt the repository workflow, its module dependencies and required
Architect/Reviewer/Bookworm configuration with Honeycomb's local-delivery
commands. Installing Busy Bee alone does not add this workflow. Dispatch each
task with `--workflow do-feature-task --cwd CANONICAL_ROOT` and explicit local
delivery authority. Keep workflow controls and helper requests in that stable
checkout while implementation and integration target the isolated task and
feature base. Coordinate canonical catalogue/tool upgrades with active runs.
Native prerequisites and Colony retain scheduling authority. Main landing,
pushes, tool installation, tracker publication and feature closure require
separate authorization.

changes.summary: expose workflow inspection and checkpoint tooling
changes.body:
Add JSON-only `system preview`, `system checkpoint` and `system schema`
interfaces for applications. Inspection combines retained actor graphs with
frozen published briefs and labelled instruction previews rendered from saved
context. Normalized invocation IDs connect invoking states to retained children.
Checkpoint reads return the run, checkpoint and update time without importing
the workflow definition.

Optional: use `busybee system --help` and the focused subcommand help when
integrating tooling. Routine agents continue to discover briefs and outcomes
through `show` and `discover`; `preview` retains structural saved-state output.
Inspection callbacks execute trusted author code without an I/O sandbox.

changes.summary: simulate workflow outcomes without advancing saved work
changes.body:
Replay original outcome data from a retained actor's saved state, or from
explicit initial input for the root actor. Validate payloads and guards, retain
untouched published briefs, and render instructions for simulated visits.
Reject stale checkpoint or definition baselines and encountered actor
coordination, timers or custom effects. Replay starts no live actors and
performs no engine writes; trusted author calculations are not sandboxed.

Optional: read `busybee system simulate --help` and
`busybee system schema --simulation --json` for the replay contract. Simulation
does not establish acceptance or completion of real work.

changes.summary: dispatch Land review visits to a dedicated reviewer
changes.body:
Land 4.1 dispatches new review visits to the `reviewer` Bee kind after the driver
records passing checks. The reviewer compares the complete scoped content and
base at the start and end, returning an approval receipt or repair findings.
Commit compares that receipt again; staging alone does not change content
identity. Retain the existing Bookworm review of exact source and squash
messages, including per-tool changelog coverage and adoption guidance.

Required when adopting this Land definition: configure the `reviewer` Bee kind
and make Colony execution available for dispatched reviews. Land 4.1 preserves
the saved 4.0 state, context and outcome contracts; already published visits
keep their frozen briefs and dispatch ownership.

adoption.text:
When adopting this Land definition: configure the `reviewer` Bee kind
and make Colony execution available for dispatched reviews. Land 4.1 preserves
the saved 4.0 state, context and outcome contracts; already published visits
keep their frozen briefs and dispatch ownership.

changes.summary: save workflow outcomes before closing stages
changes.body:
`busybee complete RUN TASK CHOICE` validates and saves the original `{choice,data}`, finishes the checkpoint write and releases its lock before attempting native closure. It supports driver-handled and Bee-dispatched visits and respects Beads acceptance and child gates.

Closure refusal or an unconfirmed closure receipt reports `stage_close_failed` with `resultSaved: true`. Inspect the task, resolve the refusal and retry with the same original choice and data. Matching retries can finish closure or acknowledge an already-closed visit, even after collection. Conflicting or malformed saved results fail, as does a closed visit without saved evidence. Drivers still advance workflows with `busybee collect RUN`.

Optional: use `complete` for ordinary stage completion after satisfying acceptance, child work and required answer delivery. Read `busybee complete --help` for payload options and prerequisites. `record-result` remains available for saving without closure; direct `next` and `choice` submissions still require an active, closed driver-handled visit.

changes.summary: read workflow tool changes without opening a tracker
changes.body:
Run `busybee changelog` for the latest recorded release. It includes
required or optional adoption guidance when recorded, without loading a
workflow, repository configuration or tracker.

Read the earlier dependency guidance with:

```sh
busybee changelog --release 0.6.0
```

That guidance describes moving workflow-only xstate and zod dependencies
to `.workflows/package.json` while retaining dependencies the application
uses. Existing root dependency setups remain valid.

adoption.text: Review the 0.6.0 dependency guidance when deciding where to install workflow-only dependencies.

changes.summary: require changelog evidence in Hive Land and Release
changes.body:
Hive's Land definition reviews exact source and final squash messages,
including every affected tool's records and adoption actions. It preserves
the final blocks and checks the actual integrated commit. Release validates
declared records, reviews generated histories and verifies offline commands
before publication. Ordinary Land leaves suite versions unchanged.

These requirements apply to Hive's Land and Release definitions, not to
all workflows run by Busy Bee. Their compatibility versions are independent
of the Hive suite version and the `changelog v1` record format.
breaking: Hive Land is now 4.0.0 and Release is now 3.0.0. Runs saved under earlier incompatible versions of those definitions cannot resume through the new mandatory changelog prerequisites.

adoption.text: When continuing an incompatible saved Hive Land or Release run, retain its authorization and evidence, inspect completed effects, and start a fresh run of the same workflow for the remaining scope.

Move workflow-only xstate and zod dependencies to .workflows/package.json, install there with your project's package manager, then verify each definition with busybee input-schema NAME --json. Retain root dependencies used by the application. Existing root dependency setups remain valid. busybee init preserves existing definitions; it does not migrate them.
